newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical industry nine-month sales down.
newsitem.headline: German chemical industry nine-month sales down.

text.p: German chemical sales improved in the third quarter of this year, but are expected to fall by one percent in the full year, the German chemical association (VCI) said on Thursday.
VCI chairman warned that the industry was unlikely to grow more than two percent in 1997.

"Forecasts of more than two percent production growth for the German chemical industry in 1997 are really on the optimistic side," Juergen Strube, head of chemical firm BASF, told a press conference at the VCI meeting.
Strube said globalisation of the chemical industry was the way forward. "Investment abroad, particularly in the emerging markets of China and South East Asia, and in the U.S. will continue."

"Europe, rather than Germany is now our home market. Two thirds of all German chemical exports go to other west European countries and about three quarters of the imports come from there," said Strube.
"The next important step is the planned European monetary union," he said.
Sales for the first three quarters, at about 135 billion marks, were about 2.5 percent lower than the previous year.
Although production in the first three quarters of 1996 was down one percent, the VCI said it expected production to rise by one percent for the whole year.
Production recovered in the third quarter after falling 3.5 percent in the first half of 1996.
The VCI said the growth impulse was coming from abroad with exports for the first three quarters at 77.5 billion marks, two percent higher than for the same time last year.
In Germany demand was depressed up until July, when it started to climb again.
The difference between business abroad and at home was reflected in returns as large international firms performed better than middle-sized players, who had to cope with pressure from cheap imports.
Strube said the acceptance of growth areas such as genetic engineering was important as well as the planned reforms of the German tax system.
Strube would not comment on the dispute over the reduction in sickpay at BASF.
